name: Priya Nair
blurb: MSc ML student writing a small LLM inference engine in her spare time.

softmax-equalizes.text: thinks softmax makes the attention weights roughly equal instead of sharpening the largest scores

sqrt-d-normalises.text: thinks dividing by the square root of d turns the scores into probabilities

kv-cache-stores-queries.text: thinks the KV cache must also keep the queries of earlier tokens

sessions.title: What does a dot product measure?

checks.q: Two unit vectors have a dot product near 1. What does that say?
o: They point in almost the same direction
checks.k: They point in almost the same direction
checks.a: They point in almost the same direction

checks.q: Q and K are both 5-by-64 (5 tokens, 64 dimensions). What shape is $QK^T$?
What do the outputs of softmax always sum to?
Scores [2, 1, 0] go through softmax. What happens to the largest score?
o: It gets the biggest share, about 0.67
All three get about one third
checks.k: It gets the biggest share, about 0.67
checks.a: All three get about one third

checks.q: Why are attention scores divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$?
o: To keep the variance of the scores near 1 so softmax doesn't saturate
To turn the scores into probabilities
checks.k: To keep the variance of the scores near 1 so softmax doesn't saturate
checks.a: To turn the scores into probabilities

checks.q: Write the scaled dot-product attention formula.
checks.k: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V
checks.a: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V

checks.q: With $d_k = 64$, what number do we divide $QK^T$ by?
Scores [4, 0] go through softmax. Roughly what weight does the first token get?
checks.k: About 0.98
checks.a: About 0.8

checks.q: Weights are $5 \times 5$, V is $5 \times 64$. What shape is the attention output?

sessions.title: How does multi-head attention split the work?

checks.q: Why use 8 heads of size 64 instead of one head of size 512?
o: Each head can attend to a different pattern
It removes the need for softmax
checks.k: Each head can attend to a different pattern
checks.a: Each head can attend to a different pattern

checks.q: d_model is 768 with 12 heads. What is each head's dimension?
If $d_k$ doubles and we forget to rescale, what happens to the softmax?
o: It gets sharper, closer to one-hot
checks.k: It gets sharper, closer to one-hot
checks.a: It gets sharper, closer to one-hot

checks.q: Random q and k entries have variance 1. What is the variance of $q \cdot k$ when $d_k = 64$?
Without positional encodings, what is self-attention blind to?
checks.k: The order of the tokens
checks.a: The order of the tokens

checks.q: Why do sinusoidal encodings use many frequencies?
o: So nearby and distant positions are both distinguishable
To make the model train faster
So every position gets the same vector
checks.k: So nearby and distant positions are both distinguishable
checks.a: To make the model train faster

sessions.title: Layer norm, residuals and the loss

checks.q: Layer norm normalises across which axis of a token's activations?
checks.k: Its feature dimension
checks.a: Its feature dimension

checks.q: Why do transformers prefer layer norm over batch norm?
checks.k: It does not depend on batch statistics, so it works for any batch size and sequence length
checks.a: Because batch size changes

checks.q: What does the residual connection give the gradient?
o: A direct path around each block
checks.k: A direct path around each block
checks.a: A direct path around each block

checks.q: The model gives the right token probability 0.25. What is the cross-entropy loss (natural log)?
What happens to the loss as the right token's probability goes to 0?
checks.k: It goes to infinity
checks.a: It goes to infinity

checks.q: A head's scores for 4 tokens are [10, 1, 1, 1]. Which best describes its attention?
o: Almost all weight on the first token
checks.k: Almost all weight on the first token
checks.a: The first token gets about 40%

sessions.title: What does the KV cache actually store?

checks.q: During generation, what does each new step add?
o: One token, attending to all earlier ones
One token, attending only to itself
checks.k: One token, attending to all earlier ones
checks.a: One token, attending to all earlier ones

checks.q: What does KV in KV cache stand for?
checks.k: keys and values
checks.a: keys and values

checks.q: Why does the cache not need earlier queries?
o: Only the newest token's query is used at each step
Queries are stored in the weights
checks.k: Only the newest token's query is used at each step
checks.a: Queries are recomputed from values

checks.q: 32 layers, d_model 4096, fp16. How many bytes of KV cache per token?
In a causal mask for 4 tokens, how many score entries are masked out?
What does the chain rule let backprop do?
o: Multiply local gradients along the path to each weight
Skip layers that are hard to differentiate
checks.k: Multiply local gradients along the path to each weight
checks.a: Multiply local gradients along the path to each weight

checks.q: y = softmax(s). Give $\partial y_i / \partial s_i$ in terms of $y_i$.
checks.k: y_i(1 - y_i)
checks.a: y_i - y_i^2

checks.q: A saturated softmax (one weight near 1) gets what kind of gradients?
o: Very small ones, so the head learns slowly
The same as an unsaturated one
checks.k: Very small ones, so the head learns slowly
checks.a: The same as an unsaturated one

checks.q: Why does the softmax Jacobian have negative off-diagonal terms?
checks.k: Raising one score must take probability mass from the others, since the outputs sum to 1

checks.q: Two heads learn identical patterns. What is lost?
o: The model can no longer use softmax
checks.k: Capacity: one head is wasted
checks.a: Capacity: one head is wasted

checks.q: For long sequences, what usually limits plain attention on a GPU?
o: Reading and writing the N × N score matrix to memory
checks.k: Reading and writing the N × N score matrix to memory
checks.a: Reading and writing the N × N score matrix to memory

checks.q: What does FlashAttention avoid storing?
o: The full N × N attention matrix
checks.k: The full N × N attention matrix
checks.a: The full N × N attention matrix

checks.q: How can softmax be computed tile by tile without seeing all scores first?
checks.k: Keep a running max and running sum, and rescale earlier partial results when the max changes
checks.a: Compute each tile's softmax and average them

checks.q: With grouped-query attention, 32 query heads share 8 KV heads. How much smaller is the cache?
checks.k: 4 times
checks.a: 8 times

checks.q: Does FlashAttention change the attention output?
o: No, it is exact; only the memory access changes
checks.k: No, it is exact; only the memory access changes
checks.a: Yes, it approximates it

links.why: Used the dot product as similarity to explain attention scores.
Treated the √d scaling and softmax as the same normalising step.
Reasoned about saturation from score variance to explain why softmax sharpens.
Sized the cache from the head dimensions she computed for multi-head attention.
Explained FlashAttention's speed through memory traffic, not arithmetic.
Mixed up what FlashAttention avoids storing with what the KV cache keeps.
